findings.text: Pre-existing manifest-honesty gap (orthogonal to the fleet-scoped AC5, which is satisfied): the byte-identical capabilities.yaml lists ~17 NON-fleet dogfood/build-machinery capabilities whose homes do NOT ship in plugin/templates - several marked 'mechanical': budget_governance (.warp/budget.py), lessons_store (.warp/lessons.py), warp_init_scaffold (.warp/init_scaffold.py), the tracker_* family (.warp/tracker_adapter.py, .warp/tracker_mirror.py, .warp/tracker_intake.py, .warp/tracker_conformance.py), pack_engine (.warp/pack.py), pack_conformance (.warp/pack_conformance.py), pack_drift_check (scripts/check_pack_drift.py), multitool_packs (.warp/packs.json), ephemeral_env_provisioning (.warp/env_provision.py), release_rollback_automation (.warp/release.py). A pack adopter gets a manifest naming modules they do not have. W5 did NOT introduce these (its capabilities.yaml diff added only the 6 fleet entries, all resolving); the spec's own AC5 phrasing 'no capability entry claims a module an adopter will not have' is met for the fleet but not manifest-wide. Recommend W6 tag dogfood/build-machinery entries distinctly (e.g. a dogfood/repo-only marker) so the SHIPPED manifest is honest end to end.

Same root cause via the /warp:init path: init_scaffold lays the byte-identical capabilities.yaml but deliberately omits ALL runtime engine (executor, metrics, events, plan, the runners, and now the fleet), so a scaffolded minimal repo's manifest over-claims capabilities whose homes it does not have. This pre-dates W5 (the engine/runner entries were already in this position) and is exactly the two-tier adoption tension the spec defers to W6 documentation. Two-tier init decision judged SOUND: keeping init_scaffold minimal and delivering the fleet via the full-engine pack path is the correct architecture (RULE #6 - expanding the proportionate scaffolder to dump the full engine would be the shortcut); the corrected AC1 ('fleet via packs, init stays minimal') honestly matches what shipped.

summary: WARP-0905 (ship the fleet in the engine, W5 of PLAN-0009) passes with notes at 2fb397f. All 6 ACs confirmed by concrete probes in an isolated umask-002 worktree: the 14-module fleet closure and bin/warp are shipped into plugin/templates and re-synced byte-identical across all 7 packs (drift empty; bin/warp blob 2508a67 100755 and dispatch.py blob 52e2d68 identical everywhere), events.py's account field is synced, capabilities.yaml is honest for all 13 fleet entries in both byte-identical copies, and the gate is GREEN (selftest 1345/0). The closure was proven CLOSED not just statically (transitive closure from bin/warp = 19 shipped modules, zero of the 11 repo-only dogfood modules reached, all 11 absent from plugin/templates) but at RUNTIME (all 14 fleet modules import standalone from an adopter-only tree; bin/warp routes with no ImportError). The drift-check teeth BITE: a mutated pack fleet module reports 'differs' and a stripped bin/warp exec bit reports 'mode', turning the gate assertion RED; the exec-bit checks are umask-independent (& 0o111 / X_OK / git-index 100755) and stayed GREEN on the umask-002 machine that broke WARP-0904. No protected path was edited and the impl commit carries no evidence files. RULE #1 clean. Two non-blocking notes flag a pre-existing manifest-honesty gap (the shipped/byte-identical capabilities.yaml lists non-fleet dogfood/build-machinery capabilities whose homes an adopter will not have) that is orthogonal to the fleet-scoped AC5 and explicitly deferred to W6. Verdict: pass_with_notes.
